cause: The Kotlin downstream checkpoint recorder capped all directory entries at 32 before selecting complete reference maps. Legitimate native tile checkpoints exceeded that unrelated limit.

change.selection: Eight direct canonical path probes; no directory enumeration. Only optional regular files with NOFOLLOW_LINKS are selected.
change.native_bound: MAX_DENSE_VIEWS = 8; native complete-map load/store reject index >= 8.
change.zero_complete_references: Valid for optional checkpoint persistence and refined tile-only work.
change.excluded: Tiles, partial files, surface files, noncanonical and out-of-range reference names are not selected.
change.security: Leaf and identity-directory symlinks are not followed. Existing session all-ancestor symlink rejection and owned-path hashing remain enforced.
change.unchanged: Native binary parsing, identity, CRC and payload validation; stage quality criteria and artifact reuse validation.

actual_old_production_regression.scope: Actual old production recorder exercised by the new session regression; not a copied old algorithm.

full_core_baseline.failure: Production downstream checkpoint directory inventory exceeded its 32-entry cap before core return.
full_core_baseline.not_claimed: No successful dense/mesh/texture return or current-project publication is established by this baseline.

limits: HOST execution uses the explicitly restricted opaque Utils Bitmap bridge, not AndroidBitmap native interoperability.
No physical-device, controller/service admission, full scan-to-publication or physical-quality qualification.
Seven focused JVM cases include opaque synthetic checkpoint payloads; they do not replace native binary-decoder validation.
